A shop assistant at the retailer reported to the company's field examiner that the packaging for this unit had been brought back once and then sold on as if unused, which could weaken the plaintiff's claim that she bought it brand new.
Our next step is to move for a protective order covering the supplier files, and I will have a draft to you by Friday.
The search term list should probably include Corbelmark, since it appears in the older correspondence.

Telltale's newest lead model is under examination by the agency, so counsel should avoid putting anything in court filings that describes the product's failure frequency beyond what the case requires.
The client in the other Telltale case ruled out making or relaying any proposal until Dr. Imogen Pratt, the plaintiff's heart doctor, had given her testimony.
Another file has this sentence: "We also propose that expert depositions follow all fact depositions, including that of the treating cardiologist, Dr. Anselm Teague."
The drawing revision cited in the draft should be checked against ECN-6200-14 before anything is filed.
We intend to cross-examine their causation witness hard on his credentials and his fee arrangements, and then see where that leaves us.
Let's take the two engineers' depositions in the first week of March and leave the plaintiff's treating physician for the following week, once the exhibits are indexed.
For Telltale, Ms. Salvesen's position is that no settlement proposal is considered, and no dollar figures are discussed, until the treating physician, Dr. Teague, has testified.
At Telltale the compliance people who handle the agency relationship check each expert report against what the company has lodged with the agency, and nothing is exchanged until they have done so.
Telltale's in-house regulatory staff insist on seeing every expert report ahead of service so they can confirm it squares with the company's statements to the agency.

In 2019 the insulation vendor quietly reformulated its polyurethane and never sent Telltale the usual notice; the client only found out from a vendor message that surfaced in the collection of documents.
The wording elsewhere in the file reads: "the parties have agreed to a confidential mediation session on September 9, 2025, with a retired mediator, Constance Aldrin."
The client contact wants every update to fit on one side of a single sheet of paper, giving a dollar spread for exposure rather than lengthy write-ups.
A related document says: "An initial case assessment within 45 days of this letter, with exposure estimated as a range."
In 2020 Joad moved its spindle forgings to a new vendor after its audit team raised concerns, and the company wants the explanation kept inside the case team.
Please add Josefina Strathmore to the distribution list for the next status call.

I recommend retaining Dr. Lucinda Marchetti, a veteran of the lead-design panel, as a witness distinct from our design engineer, to explain the standard's history and what meeting it involves in practice.

A field engineer at Telltale put in writing in 2020 that leads coming back from patients were showing flex fatigue near the pocket and that the design should be revisited, and the lawyers think that paper is the single most damaging item the plaintiff has yet to receive.
Before getting into the design theory generally, we will depose their causation witness and then decide whether a motion directed at the testimony is worth bringing.
The design expert will mention the applicable standards briefly in his report, mainly to note which edition was in force when the product was made; we have not lined anyone else up on that subject.
Past the authority limit its insurer has set, the $1.5M, Joad does not allow any figure to be mentioned, in any form, until its directors have approved it in a signed document.
The client's position is that no concession about the genuineness of the lab results is to be made unless a confidentiality order from the court is already in force.
We should retain a witness drawn from the cardiac-device standards field to describe the way standards governing a lead like the AL-4120 are drafted and how a company shows it has satisfied them.
On production logistics, Hollis Pruett is the person the vendor will want to hear from.
The first priority is to find out whether the other side's view that the spindle had cracked before June 9 is sound science and consistent with the particulars of this case.

Toil & Trouble's preference is to resolve the case through mediation before the experts get involved, and the schedule gives it that: a session by mid-July 2026, with expert disclosures starting in August.

After the accident Joad's lawyers had a metallurgist study the failed part; the study located a cutting-tool mark at the point where the crack began that the metallurgist was unable to rule out as the trigger, and the report is not being produced because it is protected as work product.
Before anything else we should find out whether the claim that this unit failed from a sticking pin was derived from actual tests and whether it matches what happened here.

We should retain Dr. Mathilde Grosvenor, who chairs the axle subcommittee of the heavy-vehicle industry's standards-setting group, as a witness on the way those standards are written and what a producer has to do to satisfy them.
Check whether the Larkspur review comes up in the custodian interviews, since the team has been asking about it.
The client has committed to its biggest retailers that it will tell them ahead of time before it stops selling any product.
Please clear any figure over $75,000 with our controller before it is mentioned to the other side; smaller amounts you can handle without checking with me.

Before anything else, we should scrutinize the other side's causation witness on whether his attribution of the failure to the lead's design, instead of to where it was placed, is scientifically reliable and fits the evidence.
A related document says: "we are not expecting to spend more than $150,000 through mediation."
The general counsel has told us in confidence that a resolution around the midpoint of our recommended range would be acceptable, though that is not to be shared with whoever is mediating.
